case_title: Ahmed Shah & Anr. v. State of Rajasthan
mitigating_circumstances: No previous deliberation or pre-meditation, sudden fight
high_court_outcome: Convicted appellants GS and AS under s.302/34 IPC, acquitted others
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused and their party were involved in a dispute over land possession. The complainant party attempted to take forcible possession of the land from the accused. During a scuffle, the accused inflicted fatal injuries on the victim. The victim was armed with a gun. The accused tried to grapple the gun from the victim. The incident resulted in the victim's death due to multiple injuries. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, medical reports, and recovered items as evidence. The trial court convicted all accused under various sections of the IPC. The High Court acquitted some accused and convicted others. The Supreme Court modified the conviction of some accused, reducing their sentence to the period already undergone.
